Tooltip_morphine: Instantly restores health, kills all pain and clears the mind, but does not heal wounds. Highly addictive.
Tooltip_naloxone: An opioid antagonist. Eases addiction, but leaves you hungry and parched.
Tooltip_fentanyl: A potent synthetic opioid. Instantly restores health and erases every wound -- injuries, fractures, scabs, stitches, fixations and patches all gone (bullets and glass shards stay; the zombie virus is untouched). Kills all pain and clears the mind. Extremely addictive.
Tooltip_oxycontin: A mild opioid painkiller. Restores some health and takes the edge off. Somewhat addictive.
Tooltip_sufentanil: A potent patch applied to the right upper arm. While it lasts it steadily eases pain and withdrawal and keeps you calm, but the addiction quietly deepens. Lasts for days; peel it off to stop.
Tooltip_methamphetamine: A powerful central nervous system stimulant. Instantly wide awake, but it won't be long before the addiction swallows you whole.
Tooltip_tranexamicacid: An antifibrinolytic. Clots the better part of every wound's bleeding, but the clot settles as extra wound severity -- the heavier the bleed, the heavier the wound left behind. Side effects: dizzy weakness, nausea and a lingering headache.
Tooltip_sulfadimidine: A sulfonamide antibiotic. Each dose burns down most of a wound infection -- heavy infections take several courses, and each one heals into a heavier wound. Does nothing against the zombie virus. Side effects: severe head pain, a fever that lingers for hours, aching kidneys and nausea.
Tooltip_dexmedetomidine: A potent sedative used in veterinary medicine for small animals -- cats, dogs and the like. It usually wipes panic and stress away completely, but animal-grade stock is a coin flip: some doses backfire into paradoxical agitation, leaving panic and stress far worse than before. Either way expect heavy drowsiness. Side effect: severe head pain.
Tooltip_GrassBandage: A rough bandage made of grass. Heals much worse than an adhesive bandage and will almost certainly infect the wound.
Tooltip_BookSplint: A splint lashed together from two books and some cloth. Works exactly like a proper splint -- stiff pages hold bone just fine.
Tooltip_TemporarySplint: A field-expedient fixation lashed from a stick, a bar or even a book with tape or wire. Right-click a fractured part in the health panel: the fracture vanishes as if it was never there -- no pain, no limp -- but the bone has not mended. Every wound on the limb hurts a little more while it stays on, and a fresh wound on that part breaks the fixation, the fracture returning at once; taking it off brings the fracture back, worse the longer it was worn. Only a full year of wear lets it heal outright.
